data:
An agent that calls an API directly has to hold the credential, which puts it in the model’s context window, its logs and its history. With gurl, the agent runs a saved request by name; gurl fills in the secrets at send time and masks them in everything it prints.
agentgurl run "get-user" --env staging {"ok":true,"status":200,"url":"https://api.example.com/users?api_key=*****","body":{"id":"u-123","auth":"Bearer *****"}, ...}
data.set-up-once-as-a-human#Set up once, as a:
The agent should only ever see names. Store secrets yourself, once:
gurl collection create "payments-api" --var BASE_URL=https://api.example.com --secret API_KEY=sk-live-... gurl save "list-payments" '{{BASE_URL}}/payments' --collection payments-api \ --auth bearer --auth-param token='{{API_KEY}}' # The agent only needs: agentgurl run "list-payments" For environments, read the secret from stdin so it never lands in shell history: gurl env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY.
data.start-here#Start here: Agent mode — turn on JSON output, no prompts and strict masking with --agent, GURL_AGENT=1 or an agentgurl symlink. Run gurl docs first. JSON output — the run --json object, dry runs, errors, history, diff and exit codes. Memory safety — why credentials must stay out of context windows, and what gurl does about it.
data.what-the-agent-sees-and-what-it-doesnt#W: Direct curl gurl in agent mode API key in the command yes no — only a request name and environment name Credential headers in output yes ***** Secrets echoed back in the response body yes ***** Secrets in error messages yes ***** Record of what happened no every run recorded with secrets masked; gurl diag

data: Agent mode makes gurl safe and predictable for an AI agent: every command that can print JSON does, nothing ever prompts, and secrets are masked everywhere, including response bodies.
data.a-recommended-agent-loop#A recommended a: agentgurl docs — learn the commands. agentgurl list, agentgurl env list, agentgurl collection list — discover what exists. agentgurl show or agentgurl collection show — inspect before running. agentgurl run --env --dry-run — check that every placeholder resolves. agentgurl run --env — run the smallest request that answers the task. On failure: agentgurl diag . Use --persist only when the task explicitly needs extracted values saved. Keep secrets out of commands: an agent should never pass a token with --var (the token is then in its context anyway). Have a human store it once in an environment or collection: gurl env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY.
data.exit-codes#Exit codes: Code Meaning 0 Success. A non-2xx response is still 0 unless --fail is passed (ok is false in the JSON). 1 Error: request or environment not found, resolution problems, transport error, script or extraction error, failed assertion, non-2xx with --fail, dry run with problems 2 Usage: missing argument with --no-input, conflicting flags (--persist --dry-run), --reveal / --output / paste / codegen --clipboard in agent mode, shell with --no-input other gurl exec exits with the child command’s code
data.no-prompts---no-input#No prompts: --no-i:
--no-input (or GURL_NO_INPUT=1) is implied by --agent and by --json. A command that would ask fails and says what to pass instead:
{"ok":false,"error":"request name is required: gurl run (list names with: gurl list --json)"} Other examples: saving into a collection that doesn’t exist, collection delete without --force, a missing passphrase (pass --passphrase or set GURL_IMPORT_PASSPHRASE), env set KEY=- on a terminal.
data.running-requests-run---json#Running requ:
stdout carries one JSON object per execution and nothing else (NDJSON for --chain steps and --data rows):
{"id":"e7770aa1-94f2-4b4a-9e3e-8605e5c1a0cc","short_id":"e7770aa1","request":"get-user","environment":"dev", "ok":true,"method":"GET","url":"http://127.0.0.1:18731/users?api_key=*****","status":200,"status_text":"OK", "duration_ms":4,"size_bytes":89,"response_headers":{"Content-Type":"application/json","Set-Cookie":"*****"}, "body":{"id":"u-123","auth":"Bearer *****"},"extracted":{"uid":"u-123"}} (Wrapped for reading; real output is one line.) The agent checks ok, reads body, and on failure reads error, failure_phase and problems, then calls gurl diag . The full field list, problem kinds and failure phases are in JSON output.
data.see-also#See also: JSON output Memory safety for AI agents gurl exec — hand an environment to a script without printing it
data.step-1-read-gurl-docs#Step 1: read gurl:
The first command an agent should run:
agentgurl docs # JSON: {"commands":[...],"sections":{...}} gurl docs # the same reference as compact text (~25KB) gurl docs run # one command It lists every command and subcommand with arguments and flags (type, default, aliases), generated from the binary itself, plus short sections on placeholders, scope precedence, extract rules, --persist, agent mode, the run --json shape, exit codes, exec and diag. See gurl docs.
data.strict-masking#Strict masking:
Outside agent mode, gurl already masks secrets in everything it shows or stores about a request: saved requests, dry runs, execution records, and the URL, headers and errors of run --json. Response bodies are shown as received, because they are your API’s data.
Agent mode also masks the body, response headers and errors, and exec output. “Secret” here means:
variables marked secret in an environment or collection, including values reached through an alias; variables whose names look sensitive (*key*, *token*, *secret*, *password*, *signature*, Authorization, Cookie, …); literal credentials written into the saved request: sensitive headers, sensitive query parameters (?api_key=…), auth params; the URL-escaped and JSON-escaped spellings of all of the above. Values shorter than 4 characters are not replaced inside free text. Details: Secret masking.
data.turn-it-on#Turn it on:
Use any one of these:
gurl --agent run "get-user" --env staging # flag, in any position GURL_AGENT=1 gurl run "get-user" # environment variable ln -s "$(command -v gurl)" ~/.local/bin/agentgurl agentgurl run "get-user" # binary named agentgurl The symlink is the most robust choice: give the agent agentgurl and it cannot forget the flag.
data.what-agent-mode-changes#What agent mode: Behaviour In agent mode Output --json is on for every command that has it: run, run --dry-run, diag, list, show, env list/show, history, timeline, diff, collection list/show, docs Prompts --no-input is on: commands never prompt; they fail and name the flag or argument to pass Errors Every error is printed on stdout as {"ok":false,"error":"..."} (and on stderr), usage errors included; help text is not printed on a usage error Masking Secrets are masked in response bodies, response headers and errors too (run, diag, diff), and in the output of exec child processes Refused (exit 2) --reveal, paste, codegen --clipboard, run --output; gurl shell refuses to start

data: Every command an agent or script needs has --json. In agent mode it is on automatically. Empty fields are omitted, and <, > and & are not escaped.
data.diag#diag: gurl diag --json prints {"record": {...}, "compared_with": ...}: the stored execution record (method, URL, headers, body, vars with name/origin/value, response headers, error, failure phase, assertions) and the comparison with the last success. See gurl diag.
data.diff#diff: gurl diff "get-user" --json {"request":"get-user", "before":{"id":"…","short_id":"699120a5","time":"…","status":200}, "after":{"id":"…","short_id":"e7770aa1","time":"…","status":200}, "format":"json","identical":true} When the responses differ, JSON bodies are compared as structured RFC 6902 changes; other bodies as a text diff.
data.errors#Errors:
With --json (or in agent mode), an error that is not part of an execution object — unknown request or environment, conflicting flags, a missing argument with --no-input — prints on stdout:
{"ok":false,"error":"request not found: nope"} The message also goes to stderr.
data.exit-codes#Exit codes: Code Meaning 0 Success. A non-2xx response is still 0 unless --fail is passed. 1 Not found, resolution problems, transport error, script or extraction error, failed assertion, non-2xx with --fail, dry run with problems 2 Usage: missing argument with --no-input, conflicting flags, refused in agent mode
data.history-and-timeline#history and timelin:
gurl history "get-user" --json gurl timeline --since 24h --json An array, newest first:
[{"id":"e7770aa1-…","short_id":"e7770aa1","request":"get-user","time":"2026-10-20T18:41:41+05:30", "ok":true,"status":200,"duration_ms":0,"size_bytes":89}, {"id":"3baa2a2c-…","short_id":"3baa2a2c","request":"get-user","time":"…","ok":false, "duration_ms":0,"size_bytes":0,"error":"variable substitution failed: …","failure_phase":"request_build"}]
data.listing-and-inspecting#Listing and inspe: Command Shape gurl list --json Array of saved requests; literal credential headers and sensitive query params masked gurl show --json One saved request, masked the same way gurl env list --json [{"name","active","variables"}] (variables = count) gurl env show --json {"name","id","variables":{...},"secrets":[...]}, secrets masked gurl collection list --json [{"name","requests","variables","updated"}] (counts) gurl collection show --json {"name","id","variables":{...},"secrets":[...],"requests":[{"name","method","url"}]}, secrets masked gurl docs --json {"commands":[{"path","usage","args","flags":[...]}],"sections":{...}} --reveal (where supported) shows the masked values, and is refused in agent mode.
data.run#run:
gurl run --json prints one object per execution on stdout and nothing else: one line for a single run, NDJSON (one line per step or row) for --chain and --data. With --persist, persisted is on the last line.
Field Meaning id, short_id Execution record id; pass to gurl diag request, collection, environment, row What ran (row for --data iterations) ok No error, no failed assertion, and a 2xx status skipped, skip_reason The request was skipped (e.g. run-if) method, url The request as sent (secrets masked) status, status_text, duration_ms, size_bytes Response summary response_headers Object of header → value; sensitive headers masked body Parsed JSON when the body is valid JSON, otherwise a string error, failure_phase Why the attempt failed problems Resolution problems: [{"kind","variable","location","message"}] assertions [{"name","passed","message"}] extracted Values captured by --extract rules persisted {"environment","variables","collections":[{"name","variables"}]} Failure phases: request_build, http, extraction, assertion, status, pre_request_script, post_response_script, run_if, next_request.
Problem kinds: missing, leftover_placeholder, bad_type, unknown_dynamic, auth.
A request that could not be resolved:
{"id":"5a9eefb8-87bc-401d-94b7-b80c9a07cf18","short_id":"5a9eefb8","request":"get-user","ok":false, "method":"GET","url":"{{BASE}}/users?api_key={{API_KEY}}","duration_ms":0,"size_bytes":0, "error":"variable substitution failed: missing required variables: BASE, API_KEY","failure_phase":"request_build", "problems":[{"kind":"missing","variable":"BASE","location":"url","message":"missing required variable \"BASE\""}, {"kind":"missing","variable":"API_KEY","location":"header Authorization","message":"missing required variable \"API_KEY\""}]} A failed assertion:
{"ok":false,"status":200,"failure_phase":"assertion", "assertions":[{"name":"status = 201","passed":false,"message":"FAIL: status = 201 (actual: 200)"}], ...} Masking matches execution records (URL, request headers, errors, response headers). Outside agent mode the body is shown as received; in agent mode secrets are masked in the body too.
data.run---dry-run---json#run --dry-run --jso:
The planned request; nothing is sent or recorded. Exits 1 when problems is non-empty.
{"dry_run":true,"request":"get-user","environment":"dev","ok":true,"method":"GET", "url":"http://127.0.0.1:18731/users?api_key=*****", "headers":[{"key":"Authorization","value":"*****"},{"key":"X-Merchant","value":"M-4242"}], "extracts":[{"name":"uid","source":"jsonpath:$.id"}]}

data: Everything that enters an LLM context window may be stored, logged, or reused in ways you don’t control. If a credential touches a context window, treat it as exposed. gurl’s job is to make sure the agent never needs to see one.
data.before-and-after#Before and after: # Before: the key is in the command, the shell history and the agent's context curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc123def456" https://api.example.com/users # After: set up once by a human gurl env create prod --var BASE_URL=https://api.example.com --var API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY gurl save "get-users" '{{BASE_URL}}/users' --auth bearer --auth-param token='{{API_KEY}}' # The agent runs agentgurl run "get-users" --env prod
data.limits#Limits: A secret has to be known to gurl to be masked: marked secret, sensitively named, or written into a credential header, sensitive query parameter or auth param. An unrelated value in a response body that happens to be sensitive is not masked. Values shorter than 4 characters are not replaced inside free text. Outside agent mode, run prints response bodies as received. Give agents agentgurl, not gurl.
data.the-layers#The layers:
1. Requests are referenced by name. The agent runs agentgurl run "get-users" --env prod. The command contains a request name and an environment name, never a value.
2. Secrets are encrypted at rest. Environment and collection secrets are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and decrypted only at send time. See Credential storage.
3. Auth is applied by gurl. Saved auth configs (--auth bearer --auth-param token='{{API_KEY}}') are filled and applied to the outgoing request inside gurl.
4. Everything gurl shows or stores is masked. show, list --json, codegen, paste, env show, dry runs, run --json URLs/headers/errors and execution records replace secret values with *****, including URL- and JSON-escaped copies. See Secret masking.
5. Agent mode masks the rest. With --agent, secrets are also masked in response bodies, response headers, errors and gurl exec child output; --reveal, paste, codegen --clipboard and run --output are refused.
$ agentgurl env show prod {"name":"prod","variables":{"API_KEY":"*****","BASE_URL":"https://api.example.com"},"secrets":["API_KEY"], ...} $ agentgurl run "whoami" --env prod {"ok":true,"status":200,"body":{"token_echo":"*****"}, ...} 6. Failures are diagnosable without secrets. Execution records never contain secret values, so gurl diag can show the agent what changed since the last success, comparing secret variables by origin only.
data.the-risks#The risks: Context exposure. A key pasted into a prompt, or printed by a command the agent ran, stays in the conversation. History and logs. Conversations and tool output are often retained. Accidental output. Models repeat what they’ve seen, for example in generated code or debugging output. Echoed secrets. APIs often echo credentials back: in a redirect URL, an error message, a debug field of the response body.

data:
For contributors and plugin authors. You don’t need this page to use gurl.
Gurl CLI is a Go binary designed for single-file distribution. The architecture follows a layered approach where each layer depends only on the layers below it.
data.9-layer-architecture#9-Layer Architectur: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ CLI (urfave/cli) │ │ save run list edit delete env collection codegen... │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Core Services │ │ Template Engine │ Auth Registry │ Formatter │ │ Curl Parser │ Scripting │ Assertions │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Storage (goleveldb) │ │ Requests │ Collections │ Environments │ History │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ HTTP Client (net/http) │ │ TLS │ Timeouts │ Proxies │ Cookie Jar │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Protocol Handlers │ │ HTTP │ GraphQL │ gRPC │ WebSocket │ SSE │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Plugin System │ │ Middleware │ Output │ Command │ Auth │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ TUI (bubbletea) — not functional │ │ Sidebar │ Request Builder │ Response Viewer │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
data.data-storage#Data Storage:
Gurl stores data in two locations:
Location Path Purpose Database ~/.local/share/gurl/gurl.db Requests, collections, environments, history Config ~/.config/gurl/config.toml User preferences, plugin settings The database uses goleveldb (LevelDB port) for high-performance key-value storage. Configuration uses TOML for human-readable settings.
data.layer-descriptions#Layer Descriptions:
CLI Layer - Uses urfave/cli for command-line argument parsing. Handles all user-facing commands like gurl save, gurl run, and gurl edit.
Core Services Layer - Contains the business logic. Request resolution (internal/resolve) turns a saved request plus its scopes into the request to send, or into the list of resolution problems; it is shared by run, collection run, the shell and the TUI. Masking rules (internal/redact) are shared by every command that shows or stores a request, and by execution records. Auth registry manages API keys, Bearer tokens, and basic auth. Formatter provides response rendering in multiple formats.
Storage Layer - goleveldb-backed persistence for requests, collections, environments, and execution history. Provides ACID-like transactions for data integrity.
HTTP Client Layer - Wraps Go’s net/http with TLS configuration, timeout handling, proxy support, and cookie jar management.
Protocol Handlers Layer - Extends beyond HTTP to support GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket, and Server-Sent Events. Each handler translates between protocol-specific formats and Gurl’s internal request/response model.
Plugin System Layer - Four plugin types: MiddlewarePlugin runs before/after requests, OutputPlugin formats responses, CommandPlugin adds new CLI commands, and AuthPlugin provides custom authentication handlers (added in v0.3.0). All plugins are discovered from ~/.config/gurl/plugins/.
TUI Layer - Built with bubbletea. The code exists but is not functional in the current release. The intended design is a full-screen three-pane workspace for browsing requests, editing them, and inspecting responses.
data.request-lifecycle#Request Lifecycle: CLI parses command and loads request from storage Pre-request scripting executes (JavaScript/goja) Request resolution fills placeholders from the scopes (environment < collection < data row < CLI < runtime) and applies auth; any problem stops the request here Middleware plugins run their ApplyBeforeRequest hooks Protocol handler sends the request Middleware plugins run their ApplyAfterResponse hooks Post-response scripting executes Assertions are evaluated Output plugin formats and displays the response The execution is recorded, with secrets masked, whether it succeeded or failed at any earlier step (inspect with gurl diag)

data: Gurl’s plugin system lets you extend functionality through middleware, output, command, and auth plugin interfaces. Go plugins are discovered from ~/.config/gurl/plugins/ and loaded into the plugin registry on startup.
data.authplugin#AuthPlugin:
Applies authentication to an outgoing request. Auth plugins expose parameter metadata through the same auth.ParamDef shape used by built-in handlers.
type AuthPlugin interface { Name() string Params() []auth.ParamDef Apply(req *client.Request, params map[string]string) error }
data.built-in-output-plugins#Built-in Output:
Plugin Description Example Output pretty Formatted JSON/XML with syntax highlighting Colored, indented output slack Slack-compatible attachment format Block kit payload markdown Markdown code blocks json ... csv Tabular data extraction Comma-separated values minimal Single-line summary 200 OK - 123ms - 2.1KB Select an output plugin with the --format flag:
gurl run "api" --format slack
data.commandplugin#CommandPlugin:
Adds new CLI commands. Use for project-specific workflows or integrations.
type CommandPlugin interface { Name() string Command() string Description() string Run(args []string) error }
data.creating-a-custom-plugin#Creating a Cust:
Custom plugins are currently low-level Go plugins, not a polished external SDK. A plugin must export a Plugin symbol whose value implements at least one known plugin interface. This example imports gurl’s internal/... packages, so build it under the gurl module tree or another module path that Go permits to import those internal packages.
Minimal middleware plugin:
package main import ( "github.com/sreeram/gurl/internal/client" "github.com/sreeram/gurl/internal/plugins" ) type HeaderPlugin struct{} func (HeaderPlugin) Name() string { return "example-header" } func (HeaderPlugin) BeforeRequest(ctx *plugins.RequestContext) *plugins.RequestContext { if ctx != nil && ctx.Request != nil { ctx.Request.Headers = append(ctx.Request.Headers, client.Header{ Key: "X-Gurl-Plugin", Value: "example-header", }) } return ctx } func (HeaderPlugin) AfterResponse(ctx *plugins.ResponseContext) *plugins.ResponseContext { return ctx } var Plugin = HeaderPlugin{} Build and place the shared object where the loader expects it:
mkdir -p ~/.config/gurl/plugins/example-header go build -buildmode=plugin -o ~/.config/gurl/plugins/example-header/example-header.so ./plugin.go The loader discovers enabled plugins at ~/.config/gurl/plugins//.so, looks up the exported Plugin symbol, and accepts values that implement MiddlewarePlugin, OutputPlugin, CommandPlugin, or AuthPlugin.
data.current-support#Current support:
The registry and loader can categorize values that implement MiddlewarePlugin, OutputPlugin, CommandPlugin, or AuthPlugin. Auth plugins are stored separately from middleware and can be listed or looked up through the registry.
External plugin packaging is still low-level Go plugin support. The loader expects plugins under ~/.config/gurl/plugins//.so and a Plugin symbol that implements at least one known plugin interface. Go plugin loading is only supported on Linux amd64 and Linux arm64.
data.middlewareplugin#MiddlewarePlugin:
Runs before and after each request. Use for logging, timing, retry logic, and request modification.
type MiddlewarePlugin interface { Name() string BeforeRequest(ctx *RequestContext) *RequestContext AfterResponse(ctx *ResponseContext) *ResponseContext }
data.outputplugin#OutputPlugin:
Formats and displays responses. Gurl includes built-in output plugins, but custom plugins can provide specialized formatting.
type OutputPlugin interface { Name() string Format() string Render(ctx *ResponseContext) string }
data.plugin-discovery#Plugin Discovery:
On startup, Gurl discovers shared objects at ~/.config/gurl/plugins//.so. If an enabled-plugin list is configured, only matching names are loaded. Each plugin file must export a Plugin symbol:
// plugin.go package main import "github.com/sreeram/gurl/..." var Plugin = MyMiddlewarePlugin{}
data.plugin-registry#Plugin Registry:
The registry stores each plugin by the interfaces it implements.
type Registry struct { middleware []MiddlewarePlugin outputs []OutputPlugin commands []CommandPlugin auths []AuthPlugin } func (r *Registry) Register(plugin interface{}) { switch p := plugin.(type) { case MiddlewarePlugin: r.middleware = append(r.middleware, p) case OutputPlugin: r.outputs = append(r.outputs, p) case CommandPlugin: r.commands = append(r.commands, p) case AuthPlugin: r.auths = append(r.auths, p) } } Auth plugins are stored separately from middleware and can be listed or looked up by name before their Apply method updates a request.
data.request-execution-touchpoints#Request ex:
During a request run, extensions can affect different parts of execution:
Middleware plugins - Can inspect or change request context before the request and response context after the response Auth handlers - Apply saved auth settings after templates are substituted and before the request is sent Output plugins - Render the response when their format is selected Custom middleware inserts into this chain via the registry.
data.security#Security:
Plugins run with the user’s permissions. Gurl applies these safeguards:
If an enabled list is configured, plugins not on that list are skipped Middleware BeforeRequest and AfterResponse calls are wrapped in panic recovery Plugin discovery treats a missing plugin directory as empty Individual plugin load failures print a warning to stderr and do not stop other plugins from loading

data: One page per command, in alphabetical order. Every page has the same layout: synopsis, flags, aliases, examples and related commands. Flag tables are checked against gurl docs --json from the binary; run gurl docs for the reference that matches your installed version.
data.commands#Commands: Command What it does auth List auth handlers and their parameters codegen Generate Go, Python, JavaScript or curl code from a request collection Manage collections, their variables, and collection runs cookies List, delete and clear stored cookies delete Remove a saved request detect Parse a curl command from stdin or a file diag Inspect one recorded execution diff Compare the latest responses of a request docs Print a compact reference of every command and concept edit Change fields of a saved request env Manage environments and their variables exec Run a command with an environment’s variables injected export Export requests to a file extract Test extraction rules against a sample response graphql Execute a GraphQL query grpc Execute a gRPC request history Show execution history for a request import Import from OpenAPI, Insomnia, Bruno, Postman, HAR or gurl exports init Initialize a project (.gurl/) list List saved requests paste Copy a request as curl to the clipboard rename Rename a saved request run Execute a saved request save Save a request under a name sequence Set execution order within a collection shell Launch the typed interactive shell show Show a saved request sse Connect to a Server-Sent Events endpoint timeline Show executions across all requests update Update gurl to the latest release ws Open a WebSocket connection gurl tui is a hidden, non-functional stub; use gurl shell for interactive use.
data.exit-codes#Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 usage error; gurl exec exits with its command’s code. Details and the JSON error shape are in JSON output.
data.global-flags#Global flags:
These work with every command, in any position.
Flag Short Description --agent JSON output, no prompts, strict masking (or GURL_AGENT=1, or run the binary as agentgurl). See Agent mode. --no-input Never prompt; fail and name what to pass instead (or GURL_NO_INPUT=1) --project-dir Project root containing .gurl file storage (or GURL_PROJECT_DIR) --version -v Print the version

data: List the built-in auth handlers and the parameters each one accepts, so you know what to pass to --auth and --auth-param on gurl save and gurl edit.
data.info#info:
Show the parameters for one auth type, marked required/optional and secret, with defaults.
gurl auth info None.
data.list#list:
List the built-in auth types.
gurl auth list None.
data.oauth-2-client-credentials#OAuth 2 clien: gurl save "service-token" https://api.example.com/service \ --auth oauth2 \ --auth-param flow=client_credentials \ --auth-param client_id='{{client_id}}' \ --auth-param client_secret='{{client_secret}}' \ --auth-param token_url='https://auth.example.com/oauth/token' \ --auth-param scope='read:orders' To change or clear saved auth, use gurl edit --auth ... or gurl edit --auth none.
data.related-commands#Related commands: gurl save - Save auth with a request gurl edit - Update or clear saved auth gurl run - Execute a request with saved auth Credential storage - Where auth params are stored
data.save-bearer-auth-that-reads-a-secret-fro: gurl save "profile" '{{BASE_URL}}/me' \ --auth bearer \ --auth-param token='{{API_KEY}}' gurl run "profile" --env prod
data.see-what-a-handler-needs#See what a hand: gurl auth info bearer Auth type: bearer Parameters: token	required,secret	Bearer token value
data.synopsis#Synopsis:
gurl auth list gurl auth info gurl run applies the auth saved on the request. Auth params may contain placeholders (token='{{API_KEY}}'); they are filled during request resolution, then the handler updates the outgoing request. Literal secret auth params are masked by show, list --json, codegen and paste.
Type Use it for basic HTTP Basic auth with username and password bearer Bearer tokens in the Authorization header apikey API key in a header or query parameter oauth1 OAuth 1.0 signed requests oauth2 OAuth 2.0 auth_code or client credentials flow awsv4 AWS SigV4 request signing digest Digest Authorization headers from supplied challenge values ntlm NTLM negotiate or challenge response headers

data: Group related requests into a collection with its own variables and encrypted secrets, run the whole collection, and share it through git or passphrase-encrypted exports.
data.create#create:
Create a collection, optionally with variables and secrets.
gurl collection create [--var KEY=VALUE ...] [--secret KEY=VALUE ...] Flag Short Default Description --var -v none Variable as KEY=VALUE (repeatable) --secret -s none Secret variable as KEY=VALUE (repeatable), encrypted at rest Aliases: add, new
data.create-a-collection-with-a-secret-and-ru: gurl collection create payments-api \ --var BASE_URL=https://api.example.com \ --secret API_KEY=sk-live-... gurl save "list-payments" '{{BASE_URL}}/payments' \ --collection payments-api \ --auth bearer --auth-param token='{{API_KEY}}' gurl collection run payments-api --env staging --bail
data.delete#delete:
Delete a collection and all of its requests. Interactive terminals ask for confirmation; with --no-input (or --json/--agent) it fails unless --force is passed.
gurl collection delete [--force] Flag Short Default Description --force false Delete without interactive confirmation Aliases: del
data.export#export:
Export a collection with passphrase-encrypted secrets.
gurl collection export --passphrase [--output ] Flag Short Default Description --output -o stdout Output file --passphrase none Passphrase for encrypting collection secrets
data.import#import:
Import a collection export, a collection directory, or .env variables.
gurl collection import [--passphrase ] [--force] gurl collection import --file .env Flag Short Default Description --force -f false Overwrite existing collection/request records --file none Path to a .env file for collection variable import --passphrase none Passphrase for decrypting collection secrets (or set GURL_IMPORT_PASSPHRASE) .env imports create the collection if needed and store values as plain (non-secret) variables. Without a passphrase and with --no-input, an encrypted import fails with passphrase required: pass --passphrase or set GURL_IMPORT_PASSPHRASE.
data.list#list:
List all collections with request and variable counts.
gurl collection list [--json] Flag Short Default Description --json -j false JSON output: [{"name","requests","variables","updated"}] Aliases: ls, l

data: Inspect one execution: the request as sent, the variables and where each came from, the response, assertions, and what changed since the last successful run of the same request.

data.inspect-a-failure#Inspect a failure: gurl diag 7e0d3985 Summary Request: failing ID: 7e0d3985 (7e0d3985-dfb2-4cb5-b886-bfd754e15e24) Environment: dev Result: FAILED: HTTP 500 Status: 500 Internal Server Error Failure phase: status Request GET http://127.0.0.1:18731/fail Variables API_KEY environment ***** BASE environment http://127.0.0.1:18731 SA_KEY environment ***** (secret) Response Status: 500 Internal Server Error Content-Type: application/json Set-Cookie: ***** ... Compared with last success No earlier successful execution of this request.
data.related-commands#Related commands: gurl run - Execute a request gurl history - List execution ids for a request gurl diff - Compare the latest responses
data.synopsis#Synopsis:
gurl diag [flags] gurl diag --id [flags] Every execution of run (single requests, --chain steps and --data rows), collection run and shell send is recorded, including failures before a response: resolution problems, connection errors and timeouts, script errors, assertion failures and non-2xx responses. Dry runs are not recorded.
A failed run prints the record id on stderr:
request failed: HTTP 500 (id: 7e0d3985) — inspect with: gurl diag 7e0d3985 collection run prints the id next to each failed request, gurl history lists ids, and run --json includes id and short_id in the JSON object. Any unique prefix of an id works.
diag prints:
Summary: request, id, time, environment, result, status, failure phase, duration and size Request: method, URL, headers and body as sent Variables: each variable with its variable origin (environment, collection, data row, CLI, runtime) and value; secrets show as ***** Response: status, headers and body (the first 4KB unless --full) Assertions: each result Compared with last success: status, duration, URL, headers and body, variable values and origins, response headers and top-level JSON fields that changed Records never contain secrets: secret and credential-looking values are masked before saving, so secret variables are compared by origin only. Response bodies are stored as received. In agent mode, diag also masks secrets in the response body and headers, using the secrets of both compared runs.

data.execution-records-and-the-failure-notice:
Every execution is recorded, including attempts that never got a response (resolution problems, connection errors, timeouts, script errors), assertion failures and non-2xx responses. Dry runs are not recorded. When a run fails, gurl names the record on stderr:
request failed: HTTP 500 (id: bbd47546) — inspect with: gurl diag bbd47546 Pass that id to gurl diag. Execution records never contain secrets; see Header Redaction.
data.exit-codes#Exit codes: Code Meaning 0 Success. A non-2xx response is still 0 unless --fail is passed. 1 Request or environment not found, resolution problems, transport error, script or extraction error, failed assertion, non-2xx with --fail, dry run with problems 2 Usage: missing request name with --no-input, conflicting flags (--persist --dry-run), --reveal or --output in agent mode
data.fail-on-non-2xx-responses#Fail on non-2x: gurl run "create-order" --env prod --fail | jq . By default a non-2xx response still exits 0. With --fail it exits 1; the body is still printed to stdout.
data.flags#Flags: Flag Short Default Description --env -e none Environment to use for variable substitution. An unknown environment is an error. --var -v none Variable as key=value (repeatable). Highest scope except runtime values. --format -f auto Output format: auto, json, or table --output -o none Write the response to a file (- for stdout). Refused in agent mode. --force false Overwrite the output file if it exists --timeout none Request timeout (e.g., 5s, 1m, 30s) --chain --ch false Enable request chaining via setNextRequest --persist false Write extracted and script-set variables back to their variable origin --dry-run false Resolve the request and print it without sending it --assert -a none Assertion to evaluate (repeatable), e.g. status=200 --fail false Exit non-zero when the response status is not 2xx (the body is still printed) --data -d none CSV or JSON data file for data-driven iteration --json -j false One JSON object per execution (NDJSON for --chain/--data), nothing else on stdout --persist and --dry-run cannot be used together (exit code 2).
data.machine-readable-output#Machine-readable:
gurl run "get-user" --env dev --json stdout gets one JSON object per execution (one line). Empty fields are omitted:
{"id":"50488e65-9cb3-4cbe-a5b2-769258964b6e","short_id":"50488e65","request":"get-user","environment":"dev", "ok":true,"method":"GET","url":"http://127.0.0.1:18731/users?api_key=*****","status":200,"status_text":"OK", "duration_ms":4,"size_bytes":89,"response_headers":{"Content-Type":"application/json","Set-Cookie":"*****"}, "body":{"id":"u-123"},"extracted":{"uid":"u-123"}} (Wrapped here for reading; the real output is one line.)
The full set of fields is:
id short_id request collection environment row ok skipped skip_reason method url status status_text duration_ms size_bytes response_headers body error failure_phase problems[{kind,variable,location,message}] assertions[{name,passed,message}] extracted persisted{environment,variables,collections[{name,variables}]} ok is true when there was no error, no failed assertion and the status was 2xx. body is the parsed JSON value when the body is valid JSON, otherwise a string. A failed attempt has error and failure_phase: request_build, http, extraction, assertion, status, pre_request_script, post_response_script, run_if or next_request. Requests that cannot be resolved list structured problems. Problem kinds are missing, leftover_placeholder, bad_type, unknown_dynamic and auth: {"ok":false,"failure_phase":"request_build","error":"variable substitution failed: missing required variables: BASE, API_KEY", "problems":[{"kind":"missing","variable":"BASE","location":"url","message":"missing required variable \"BASE\""}, ...]} --chain steps and --data rows each print one line (NDJSON). With --persist, persisted is on the last line. Masking matches execution records: secret values are masked in the URL, request data, response headers and errors. The body is shown as received, except in agent mode, where secrets are masked in the body too. The failure notice is not printed with --json; the record id is in the object (id, short_id). With --json, errors before any execution (unknown request or environment, conflicting flags) print {"ok":false,"error":"..."} on stdout, as well as the message on stderr. --dry-run --json prints the planned request instead:
{"dry_run":true,"request":"get-user","environment":"dev","ok":true,"method":"GET", "url":"http://127.0.0.1:18731/users?api_key=*****", "headers":[{"key":"Authorization","value":"*****"},{"key":"X-Merchant","value":"M-4242"}], "extracts":[{"name":"uid","source":"jsonpath:$.id"}]}
data.output-streams#Output streams: The response body goes to stdout. Status lines, notes (for example note: uid not saved; add --persist to use them in later runs), persist summaries, assertion summaries and Response saved go to stderr, so gurl run ... | jq . sees only the body. With --json, stdout carries only JSON (see below).
data.persist-flow-variables#Persist flow vari:
gurl run "login" --chain --persist --env staging Without --persist, extracted and script-set variables are dropped at the end of the run and run prints a note naming them. With --persist, each one is written back to its variable origin: values that came from the environment go to the environment (--env or the active one), others to the request’s collection, otherwise to the environment. CLI variables and data-row values are not written back unless extraction or a script changes them.
--persist refuses to write a value that contains {{ (for example refusing to persist "tpl": value contains "{{"), and returns an error for a locked collection instead of overwriting it.
data.preview-without-sending-dry-run#Preview: gurl run "get-user" --env dev --dry-run GET http://127.0.0.1:18731/users?api_key=***** Authorization: ***** X-Merchant: M-4242 extract: uid <- jsonpath:$.id The dry run shows the request after pre-request scripts run, with secrets masked. It never applies auth (applying auth could contact a token endpoint), leaves {{$uuid}}-style dynamic functions in place, sends nothing, records nothing, and exits 1 when the request has resolution problems.

data.run-a-chained-request#Run a chained requ: gurl run "login" --chain --env staging Enables request chaining for saved post-response scripts that call gurl.setNextRequest(...). Extracted variables and variables set by scripts become available to later requests in the chain.
data.run-a-request-with-saved-auth#Run a requ: gurl save "profile" https://api.example.com/me \ --auth bearer \ --auth-param token='{{token}}' gurl run "profile" --var token=abc123 The saved bearer auth handler adds the Authorization: Bearer abc123 header during execution. You don’t need to resupply --auth when running the request.
data.synopsis#Synopsis:
gurl run [flags] The run command executes a request that was previously saved with gurl save. You can pick an environment, override variables, set timeouts, validate responses with assertions, iterate over a data file, and follow request chains.
Before anything is sent, gurl performs request resolution: every {{placeholder}} in the URL, headers, body and auth params is filled from the scopes (environment < collection < data row < CLI --var < runtime). If any placeholder cannot be filled, the request is not sent and every resolution problem is reported at once, for example missing required variables: BASE, API_KEY. See Environments and variables for the placeholder rules.
If the saved request has auth settings, gurl run applies them after the placeholders are filled.

Install gurl, then follow the quickstart: save a request, run it, move its values into an environment, and group requests in a collection.
Installation — Homebrew, install script, container image, binaries, or source. Quickstart — save → run → environment → collection.
gurl ships as a single static binary with no runtime dependencies. Pick one install method, then verify and continue to the Quickstart.
data.install#Install:
HomebrewScriptBinaryDockerSource macOS and Linux:
brew tap bsreeram08/gurl https://github.com/bsreeram08/gurl brew install gurl curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bsreeram08/gurl/master/scripts/install.sh | bash Detects your platform, downloads the matching binary from the latest release , and installs it to /usr/local/bin.
Download from GitHub Releases :
# macOS (Apple Silicon) curl -LO https://github.com/bsreeram08/gurl/releases/latest/download/gurl-darwin-arm64.tar.gz tar -xzf gurl-darwin-arm64.tar.gz && sudo mv gurl /usr/local/bin/gurl # Linux (x86_64) curl -LO https://github.com/bsreeram08/gurl/releases/latest/download/gurl-linux-amd64.tar.gz tar -xzf gurl-linux-amd64.tar.gz && sudo mv gurl /usr/local/bin/gurl # Linux (ARM64) curl -LO https://github.com/bsreeram08/gurl/releases/latest/download/gurl-linux-arm64.tar.gz tar -xzf gurl-linux-arm64.tar.gz && sudo mv gurl /usr/local/bin/gurl Each release also includes raw binaries and SHA256SUMS.
Every release tag publishes a multi-arch image (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) to GitHub Container Registry: ghcr.io/bsreeram08/gurl:latest (newest stable release; pre-releases don’t move it) and one tag per release, matching the GitHub release tag, e.g. v0.7.0.
docker run --rm ghcr.io/bsreeram08/gurl:latest --version docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work ghcr.io/bsreeram08/gurl:latest list docker run --rm ghcr.io/bsreeram08/gurl:v0.7.0 --version # pinned, reproducible Keep the database, project files and key material across runs by mounting the host directories:
docker run --rm \ -v "$PWD:/work" \ -v "$HOME/.local/share/gurl:/home/gurl/.local/share/gurl" \ -v "$HOME/.config/gurl:/home/gurl/.config/gurl" \ -w /work \ ghcr.io/bsreeram08/gurl:latest list The package is public. If GitHub still shows it as private, log in with a token that has read:packages: echo "$GHCR_TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io -u "$GITHUB_USER" --password-stdin.
Requires Go 1.25.0+.
git clone https://github.com/bsreeram08/gurl.git cd gurl go build -o gurl ./cmd/gurl sudo mv gurl /usr/local/bin/gurl

Path set in $GURL_CONFIG_PATH .gurlrc (current directory) ~/.gurlrc ~/.config/gurl/config.toml [general] history_depth = 100 auto_template = true timeout = "30s" [output] default_format = "auto" syntax_highlight = true json_pretty = true

data: Five minutes, five steps: save → run → environment → collection → inspect. Every command below works against the public jsonplaceholder.typicode.com API.
data.group-requests-in-a-collection#Group req: gurl collection create "users-api" --var id=1 gurl edit "get-user" --collection users-api gurl edit "list-users" --collection users-api gurl collection run "users-api" --env dev Collection variables sit above environment variables and below --var. A collection run executes its requests in order (see gurl sequence).
data.inspect-what-happened#Inspect what happe:
Every run is recorded, including failures:
gurl history "get-user" # short ids, status, duration gurl diag # request as sent, variable origins, response, changes since last success
data.move-values-into-an-environment#Move val:
Hard-coded hosts and tokens don’t belong in saved requests. Use {{placeholders}} and put the values in an environment:
gurl env create dev \ --var BASE_URL=https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com \ --var API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY # KEY=- reads the value from stdin, without echo gurl save "get-user" '{{BASE_URL}}/users/{{id}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{API_KEY}}' gurl run "get-user" --env dev --var id=1 Secret values are encrypted at rest and shown as ***** by gurl env show dev. If a placeholder can’t be filled, gurl refuses to send the request and names every missing variable. See Variables & placeholders.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Environments & secrets and Variables & placeholders Chaining & extraction — log in once, reuse the token Agent mode — let an AI agent run your requests without seeing secrets CLI reference — every command and flag
data.run-it#Run it:
gurl run "list-users" The response body goes to stdout; status lines and notes go to stderr, so piping works:
gurl run "list-users" | jq '.[0].email' Add assertions, or make non-2xx responses fail the command:
gurl run "list-users" --assert "status=200" --fail
data.save-a-request#Save a request:
gurl save "list-users" https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users A saved request has a name, a method, a URL, and optional headers, body, auth and extraction rules. You can also paste a curl command:
gurl save "create-user" --curl "curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"name\":\"Ada\"}' https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users" Check what you saved:
gurl list gurl show "create-user"

data:
Each guide covers one task end to end. Read them in order the first time; later, jump to the one you need.
Guide Read it when you want to… Environments & secrets keep hosts and credentials out of saved requests, switch dev/staging/prod Variables & placeholders understand {{placeholders}}, typed and dynamic values, scope precedence, --persist Chaining & extraction pull a token or id out of one response and use it in the next request Collections & data-driven runs run a group of requests in order, feed CSV/JSON rows, produce CI reports Diagnosing failures find out why a run failed and what changed since it last worked Scripting & assertions check responses, or run JavaScript before and after a request Other protocols call GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket or SSE endpoints
Extraction rules capture values from a response; chaining runs the next request with those values. Together they turn “log in, then call the API with the token” into one command.
data.1-write-and-test-an-extraction-rule#1. W:
A rule has the form VAR=METHOD:EXPR:
Method Captures Example jsonpath A JSONPath value (array indexes supported) orderId=jsonpath:$.data.items[0].id jq Alias of jsonpath token=jq:$.token header A response header location=header:Location regex The first capture group n=regex:"amount":(\d+) Test it against a sample response first. No request is sent:
echo '{"token":"t-123","user":{"id":42}}' | gurl extract 'token=jsonpath:$.token' 'uid=jsonpath:$.user.id' token = t-123 uid = 42 See gurl extract.
data.2-save-the-rule-on-the-request#2. Save t:
gurl save "login" '{{BASE_URL}}/auth/login' -X POST \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"user":"{{USER}}","password":"{{PASSWORD}}"}' \ --extract 'token=jsonpath:$.token' # or add it to an existing request gurl edit "login" --extract 'token=jsonpath:$.token' Run it with --json to see what was extracted:
gurl run "login" --env dev --json | jq .extracted
data.3-chain-to-the-next-request#3. Chain to:
A post-response script picks the next request with gurl.setNextRequest. Run the first request with --chain:
gurl edit "login" --post-script 'gurl.setNextRequest("profile")' gurl save "profile" '{{BASE_URL}}/me' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{token}}' gurl run "login" --env dev --chain Extracted and script-set values are runtime values: the highest scope, available to every later request, assertion, script and run-if check in the same run. With --json, each step prints one line (NDJSON).
Skip a step conditionally with a saved run-if expression (VAR == VALUE or VAR != VALUE; missing variables count as empty):
gurl edit "profile" --run-if "token != ''"
Runtime values are dropped at the end of the run, and run prints a note naming them. Add --persist to write them back to their variable origin:
gurl run "login" --env dev --chain --persist --persist refuses values that contain {{ and locked collections. Details: Variables & placeholders.
data.see-also#See also: Collections & data-driven runs — chains across a whole collection Scripting & assertions — the script API

data: A collection groups saved requests and carries its own variables and secrets. gurl collection run executes its requests in order, once per iteration or data row, and reports pass/fail for each.
data.build-a-collection#Build a collection: gurl collection create "checkout" --var CURRENCY=EUR --secret API_KEY=sk-test-... gurl save "create-order" '{{BASE_URL}}/orders' -X POST -c checkout \ --extract 'orderId=jsonpath:$.id' gurl save "capture-payment" '{{BASE_URL}}/orders/{{orderId}}/capture' -X POST -c checkout gurl collection show "checkout" # requests and variables (secrets masked) Collection variables sit between environment and data-row values in scope precedence, and may reference environment keys (API_URL={{BASE_URL}}/v1).
data.data-driven-runs#Data-driven runs:
Feed rows from CSV or JSON; each row is one iteration, and its columns become data-row variables:
email,name alice@example.com,Alice bob@example.com,Bob gurl collection run "signup" --data users.csv --env staging gurl run "create-user" --data users.json # a single request works too JSON data is an array of objects: [{"email": "alice@example.com", "name": "Alice"}].
Repeat without data using --iterations 3, and pace requests with --delay 200ms.
data.file-backed-reloads#File-backed reloads: For project-backed collections (gurl init, gurl collection migrate), a long collection run watches the collection files. The current iteration always uses the snapshot it started with; changes (debounced) apply from the next iteration or data row.
data.flow-variables-across-requests#Flow vari:
Extraction rules and scripts share one map of runtime values. A value extracted by one request is available to later requests’ placeholders, assertions, scripts and run-if checks:
gurl edit "create-order" --post-script "gurl.setNextRequest('capture-payment')" gurl edit "capture-payment" --run-if "orderId != ''" Write them back to their variable origin at the end of the run with --persist (not combinable with --dry-run):
gurl collection run "checkout" --env staging --persist See Chaining & extraction.
data.preview-then-run#Preview, then run:
gurl collection run "checkout" --env staging --dry-run gurl collection run "checkout" --env staging A dry run prints the request order and each resolved request without sending anything, running post-response scripts, recording history, writing reports or persisting variables.
A failed request prints its execution id on stderr, ready for gurl diag:
[FAIL] capture-payment: HTTP 500 (id: 01dda65f) — inspect with: gurl diag 01dda65f gurl collection run exits 1 when any request fails.
data.reports-for-ci#Reports for CI:
Reporters are console, junit, json and html; repeat --reporter for several. Files go to --reporter-output DIR (as report.xml, report.json, …). Create the directory first:
mkdir -p reports gurl collection run "api-tests" --env ci --reporter junit --reporter json --reporter-output reports --ci # GitHub Actions - name: Run API tests run: | mkdir -p reports gurl collection run "api-tests" --env ci --reporter junit --reporter-output reports --bail - name: Publish test results uses: dorny/test-reporter@v1 with: name: API tests path: reports/report.xml reporter: java-junit Add --verbose to print request and response headers and bodies for each request.
data.see-also#See also: gurl collection — every subcommand and flag, including sharing collections through git with passphrase-encrypted secrets gurl sequence
data.set-the-order#Set the order: gurl sequence set "create-order" 1 gurl sequence set "capture-payment" 2 gurl sequence list "checkout"
data.stop-early#Stop early: Flag Effect --bail Stop on the first failure of any kind; remaining requests are skipped --assert-bail Stop on the first failed assertion only --ci CI mode: treat skipped requests as failures (exit 1)

data: Every execution is recorded, so when a request fails you don’t need to re-run it with extra flags: look it up by id and compare it with the last time it worked.
data.1-get-the-execution-id#1. Get the execut:
A failed run prints it on stderr:
request failed: HTTP 500 (id: 078b9896) — inspect with: gurl diag 078b9896 Other ways to find it:
gurl history "health" # newest first, with short ids and errors gurl history "health" --json # [{"id","short_id","request","time","ok","status",...}] gurl timeline --since 1h # across all requests gurl run "health" --json | jq -r .short_id
data.2-inspect-it#2. Inspect it:
gurl diag 078b9896 # any unique prefix works; or: gurl diag --id 078b9896 diag shows:
Summary: result, status, failure phase (request_build, http, extraction, assertion, status, pre_request_script, post_response_script, run_if, next_request), duration, size Request as sent Variables, each with its variable origin (environment, collection, data, cli, or a runtime value) — secret values show as ***** Response headers and body (first 4KB; --full for all of it) Assertions Compared with last success: what changed since the last successful run of the same request — status, duration, URL, headers and body, variable values and origins, response headers and top-level JSON fields --json prints the record and the comparison as JSON.
data.3-read-the-failure-phase#3. Read the fai: Phase Usually means Next step request_build A placeholder couldn’t be filled Check the problems list; gurl run --dry-run http Connection error or timeout Host, network, --timeout status Non-2xx response Response body in diag; compare with last success assertion An --assert failed Assertion messages in diag extraction An --extract rule found nothing Test the rule with gurl extract on the stored body pre_request_script / post_response_script A script threw Script error in diag
data.compare-the-latest-responses#Compare the: gurl diff "health" # last two responses gurl diff "health" --json # structured RFC 6902 changes, or a text diff
data.secrets-in-records#Secrets in records: Records never contain secrets: secret and credential-looking values are masked before saving, so diag compares secret variables by origin only (“came from environment both times”), never by value. In agent mode, diag and diff also mask secrets in response bodies and headers, using the secrets of both compared runs.

data.what-gets-recorded#What gets recorded:
Every execution of run (single requests, --chain steps, --data rows), collection run and shell send, including attempts that never got a response:
resolution problems (missing variables, bad types) connection errors and timeouts pre-request and post-response script errors failed assertions and non-2xx responses Dry runs are not recorded. Records store the method, URL, headers, body, variables with their origins, response headers, error, failure phase and assertion results, with secrets masked before saving. Response bodies are stored as received.

data: An environment is a named set of variables, such as BASE_URL and API_KEY, that fills the {{placeholders}} in saved requests at send time. Keep one environment per stage and the same saved requests work against all of them.
data.alias-keys-across-environments#Alias key:
Two environments may name the same credential differently. An alias is an environment value that refers to another key of the same environment:
gurl env set nets-beta 'API_KEY={{SA_KEY}}' Requests that use {{API_KEY}} now get the value of SA_KEY in nets-beta. Aliases resolve one level only (no re-expansion). When a request uses the alias, the resolved value is masked like the secret it points to.
data.create-an-environment#Create an environm: gurl env create dev --var BASE_URL=https://dev.api.example.com --var TIMEOUT=30 gurl env create prod --var BASE_URL=https://api.example.com
data.environment-commands#Environment command: Command Description gurl env create Create an environment (--var KEY=VALUE, --var KEY=-, --secret KEY) gurl env list List environments (--json) gurl env show Show variables, secrets masked (--json, --reveal) gurl env set KEY=VALUE Set variables (KEY=- reads stdin) gurl env unset --var KEY Remove a variable gurl env switch Make an environment active gurl env import --file .env Import a .env file gurl env delete Delete an environment Full flags: gurl env. Next: Variables & placeholders explains how environment values combine with collection, data-row and --var values.
data.hand-an-environment-to-another-tool#Hand:
gurl exec runs a command with the environment’s variables in its process environment, without printing them:
gurl exec --env prod -- node e2e.mjs gurl exec --env prod -- sh -c 'curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "$BASE_URL/v1/charges"'
data.store-a-secret-without-typing-it-on-the-:
Mark a variable secret with --secret KEY. Pass the value as KEY=- to read it from stdin; on a terminal gurl prompts without echo, so the value never lands in shell history:
gurl env create prod --var BASE_URL=https://api.example.com --var API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY # or later: gurl env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY printf '%s' "$PROD_KEY" | gurl env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY gurl env set prod KEY - (a lone -) is rejected: use KEY=-.
Secret values are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM (see Credential storage) and shown as *****:
gurl env show prod # secrets masked gurl env show prod --json # {"name","id","variables":{...},"secrets":[...]}, masked gurl env show prod --reveal # plaintext; refused in agent mode gurl env list --json # [{"name","active","variables"}] --reveal prints secrets in plaintext to your terminal and its scrollback. Don’t use it while screen-sharing, in CI logs, or in a session an AI agent can read. It is refused in agent mode.
data.use-an-environment#Use an environment:
Reference variables as {{NAME}} in the URL, headers, body or auth params of a saved request:
gurl save "list-charges" '{{BASE_URL}}/v1/charges' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{API_KEY}}' gurl run "list-charges" --env prod # one run gurl env switch prod # make prod the active environment gurl run "list-charges" --env with an unknown name is an error; gurl never silently runs without variables.

data: Saved requests are HTTP. For other protocols gurl has one-shot commands that take the endpoint as an argument. They are not saved, recorded, or filled from environments.
data.graphql#GraphQL: gurl graphql https://api.example.com/graphql --query '{ users { name email } }' gurl graphql https://api.example.com/graphql \ --query 'query($limit: Int!) { users(limit: $limit) { name } }' \ --vars '{"limit": 10}' gurl graphql https://api.example.com/graphql --query-file queries/get-users.graphql --op GetUsers To keep a GraphQL call with auth and environments, save it as an ordinary POST request with a JSON body ({"query": "...", "variables": {...}}) and run it with gurl run. Flags: gurl graphql.
data.grpc#gRPC: gurl grpc localhost:50051 --list # services via reflection gurl grpc localhost:50051 --service UserService --method GetUser --data '{"id": 1}' TLS options: --cacert, --cert, --key, --server-name, or --insecure for testing. Flags: gurl grpc.
data.server-sent-events#Server-Sent Events: gurl sse https://api.example.com/events --event order.created --json Flags: gurl sse.
data.websocket#WebSocket: gurl ws wss://echo.example.com --send '{"type":"ping"}' # send one message and exit gurl ws wss://echo.example.com --pretty --timestamp # interactive (stdin/stdout) Flags: gurl ws.

data: Assertions check a response without code; scripts run JavaScript before a request is sent and after its response arrives. Start with assertions and reach for a script only when you need logic.
data.assertions#Assertions:
Pass one or more --assert flags to run (all must pass), or save them on a request with gurl edit --assert:
gurl run "get-user" --assert "status=200" --assert "body.$.email contains @" gurl edit "get-user" --assert "status=200" A failed assertion makes run exit 1, records the execution with failure phase assertion, and prints the failure notice with the execution id. With --json, results are in "assertions":[{"name","passed","message"}].
data.example-capture-a-value-and-pick-the-nex: var data = gurl.response.json(); if (data.requiresProfile) { gurl.setVar("USER_ID", String(data.userId)); gurl.setNextRequest("get-profile"); }
data.example-validate-inside-a-script#Example: var data = gurl.response.json(); gurl.test("has users", function () { gurl.expect(data.status).to.equal("success"); });
data.examples#Examples: # Validation error is returned as expected gurl run "invalid-order" --assert "status=400" --assert "body contains validation" # Header present and fast enough gurl run "health" --assert "headers.X-Request-Id exists" --assert "time<500" # Extraction worked gurl run "login" --assert "extract:token != ''"
data.sandbox#Sandbox:
Scripts cannot read secret variables unless explicitly allowed, and URL changes are limited to http and https. See Security.
Tip Keep scripts small. If a script grows past a few lines, the logic probably belongs in your application or test code; use gurl exec to hand it an environment instead.
data.script-api#Script API:
Everything hangs off the global gurl object:
API Description gurl.request.headers.get(name) / .set(name, value) / .remove(name) Read or change request headers (pre-request) gurl.request.url, gurl.request.body, gurl.request.method Read or assign the URL, body and method gurl.response.status, .statusText, .time, .size, .body Response fields (post-response) gurl.response.json(), gurl.response.text() Parsed JSON body, raw text body gurl.response.headers.get(name) Response header gurl.setVar(name, value), gurl.getVar(name) Set or read a runtime variable gurl.setNextRequest(name) Run this saved request next (with run --chain or in a collection run) gurl.skipRequest() Skip the current request gurl.test(name, fn), gurl.expect(value).to.equal(expected) Named checks inside a script console.log, console.warn, console.error Logging Variables set with gurl.setVar are runtime values: the highest scope, available to later requests in the same run, and written back only with --persist (which refuses values containing {{). See Variables & placeholders.
data.scripts#Scripts:
Scripts are JavaScript (the goja runtime, ECMAScript 5.1+) saved on the request as inline source:
gurl save "login" '{{BASE_URL}}/login' -X POST --extract 'token=jsonpath:$.token' \ --post-script 'gurl.setNextRequest("profile")' gurl edit "profile" --pre-script 'gurl.request.headers.set("X-Request-Time", String(Date.now()))' Pre-request scripts run before the request is sent: add headers, rewrite the URL or body, or skip the request. Post-response scripts run after the response arrives: read the body, set variables, add tests, choose the next request.
data.see-also#See also: Chaining & extraction gurl run, gurl edit
data.syntax#Syntax:
Comparison operators attach directly to the field; word operators are surrounded by spaces:
status=200 status>=200 time<1000 body contains success body not_contains error body matches u-\d+ headers.X-Request-Id exists Operator Meaning =, != Equal, not equal <, >, <=, >= Numeric comparison contains, not_contains Substring match matches Regular expression match exists Field is present and non-empty (no value) Field Value status (or status_code) HTTP status code headers.NAME Response header, e.g. headers.Content-Type contains json body Whole response body as text body.$.path JSONPath into the body, e.g. body.$.data.items[0].id = 7 (body.data.id also works) extract:NAME A value extracted or set by a script, e.g. extract:orderId != '' time Response time in milliseconds size Response size in bytes An assertion that can’t be parsed (invalid assertion format) stops the run with exit code 1 before anything is sent.

data: A placeholder is a {{name}} marker in a saved request’s URL, headers, body or auth params. Request resolution replaces every placeholder with a value at send time, or stops the request and lists every problem. Nothing with an unresolved placeholder is ever sent.
data.dynamic-functions#Dynamic functions: Function Value {{$uuid}} Random UUID {{$timestamp}} Unix timestamp (seconds) {{$isoTimestamp}} ISO 8601 timestamp {{$randomInt(1,100)}} Random integer in the range {{$randomString(8)}} Random string of the given length {{$randomEmail}} Random email address Dynamic functions work in run, collection run, the shell and auth params. A dry run leaves them in place. An unknown function ({{$nope}}) is a resolution problem.
data.environment-aliases#Environment aliases: An environment value can name another key of the same environment: API_KEY={{SA_KEY}}. See Environments & secrets.
data.keeping-runtime-values---persist#Keeping:
Values extracted from a response (--extract) or set by a script (gurl.setVar) live only for the current run. Without --persist, run drops them and prints a note such as note: uid not saved; add --persist to use them in later runs.
With --persist, each extracted or script-set value is written back to its variable origin:
a variable that came from the environment goes to that environment (--env or the active one); otherwise it goes to the request’s collection, or to the environment if the request has no collection. --persist refuses:
a value that contains {{ (refusing to persist "tpl": value contains "{{"), so placeholders never get stored as values; a locked (passphrase-protected, not unlocked) collection, instead of overwriting it; --dry-run (exit code 2). CLI --var values and data-row values are never written back unless an extraction or a script changes them.
data.placeholder-forms#Placeholder forms: Form Meaning Example {{name}} Plain value, inserted as text {{BASE_URL}}/users/{{id}} {{name:num}} Must be a number {"amount": {{amount:num}}} {{name:bool}} Must be true or false {"live": {{live:bool}}} {{name:raw}} Inserted as-is (e.g. a JSON fragment) {"meta": {{meta:raw}}} {{$fn}} Dynamic function, computed per send {{$uuid}}
data.see-also#See also: Chaining & extraction gurl run and gurl docs (its “Placeholders” and “Scope precedence” sections are the short version of this page)
data.typed-placeholders-keep-json-bodies-vali:
A bare {{amount:num}} makes the stored body invalid JSON. Quote it instead: in a JSON body, the quoted form "{{amount:num}}" (likewise "{{x:bool}}" and "{{x:raw}}") drops the quotes when it is filled.
gurl save "charge" '{{BASE_URL}}/charges' -X POST \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"amount":"{{amount:num}}","capture":"{{capture:bool}}"}' gurl run "charge" --env dev --var amount=5 --var capture=true --dry-run POST https://dev.api.example.com/charges Content-Type: application/json {"amount":5,"capture":true} A value of the wrong type is a resolution problem (variable "amount" must be a number); the value itself is never echoed in the error.
data.when-resolution-fails#When resolution fa:
Every problem is collected and reported at once, and the request is not sent:
Error: variable substitution failed: missing required variables: BASE, API_KEY Problem kind Cause missing No scope has a value for {{name}} leftover_placeholder A value still contains a placeholder, e.g. --var 'API_KEY={{other}}'. Values are filled in one pass and never re-expanded. bad_type A typed placeholder got the wrong kind of value unknown_dynamic {{$fn}} is not a known function auth The auth config cannot be resolved With run --json, these appear as structured problems entries (kind, variable, location, message). Use --dry-run to check a request without sending it; it exits 1 when there are problems.
data.where-values-come-from-scopes#Where valu:
Each value comes from one scope. When the same name is set in several scopes, the higher one wins:
Scope (lowest first) Set with 1. Environment --env NAME or gurl env switch NAME 2. Collection gurl collection create/set-var (the request’s collection) 3. Data row --data rows.csv / rows.json 4. CLI --var key=value 5. Runtime values extracted from a response or set by a script earlier in the same run The scope a variable’s final value came from is its variable origin. gurl diag shows the origin of each variable in a recorded execution, and --persist uses it to decide where to write values back.
Collection values may reference environment keys, so one collection can serve several environments:
gurl env create staging --var BASE_URL=https://staging.example.com gurl collection create "users-api" --var 'API_URL={{BASE_URL}}/v1'

data:
gurl is built on one principle: credentials stay on your machine and out of anything gurl prints or stores.
Page Covers Credential storage AES-256-GCM encryption of environment and collection secrets, machine and collection keys, sharing secrets with a passphrase Secret masking What counts as a secret, where it is masked, --reveal, agent mode, execution records
data.code-generation-safety#Code generation s: All code generators (curl, Python, JavaScript, Go) escape values for the target language, preventing shell or code injection. codegen -l curl quotes each header as one argument (-H 'Content-Type: application/json'), masks literal secrets unless --reveal, and always replaces Authorization with a placeholder.
data.core-properties#Core properties:
Secrets are encrypted at rest. Environment and collection variables marked secret are encrypted with AES-256-GCM. The machine key is generated with crypto/rand on first use and stored with owner-only permissions; encrypted values are useless on another machine.
Secrets are entered without echo. gurl env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY reads the value from stdin, prompting without echo on a terminal.
Auth is applied inside gurl. Saved auth configs are filled from placeholders and applied to the outgoing request; the calling process never builds the credential string.
Output is masked. show, list --json, codegen, paste, env show, dry runs and run --json replace secrets with *****, including their URL- and JSON-escaped forms. Agent mode also masks response bodies, headers, errors and gurl exec child output.
Execution records never store secrets. Every run is recorded for gurl diag, with secrets masked before saving.
Layer What it handles Where secrets live Environment and collection secrets Encrypted storage and retrieval AES-256-GCM at rest Auth handlers Credential injection at send time In memory only Output and execution records Masked display and auditing Never: replaced with *****
data.path-protection#Path protection: Export and import commands validate file paths to prevent directory traversal; paths containing .. are rejected. Temporary files used during self-update are created with os.CreateTemp.
data.scripting-sandbox#Scripting sandbox: The JavaScript runtime restricts secret variable access by default: scripts cannot read secrets unless explicitly granted access. URL changes made by scripts are limited to http and https.

data: Gurl separates secret storage from general configuration. Secrets are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM with a machine-specific key. General settings live in a plain TOML config file with no credentials.
data.auth-credentials-in-requests#Auth Creden:
Saved requests store auth configuration in a goleveldb database at ~/.local/share/gurl/gurl.db. Save or edit auth with --auth and repeated --auth-param key=value flags.
Database: goleveldb (LevelDB port, memory-mapped, transactional)
Auth params: Values are stored as JSON in SavedRequest.AuthConfig. If you put a literal password or token in --auth-param (or a literal Authorization header, or ?api_key=… in the URL), it is saved in the request database in plaintext. gurl masks such literals in show, list --json, codegen, paste and dry runs (see Secret masking), but masking is not encryption. Prefer placeholders that point at encrypted secrets, such as --auth-param token='{{API_TOKEN}}'.
Permissions: Database file has owner-only permissions by default
At execution time, gurl substitutes templates in auth parameters before the auth handler applies credentials to the outgoing request. Saved auth can be replaced with gurl edit --auth ... or cleared with gurl edit --auth none.
Future: Keychain integration for macOS and Windows is under consideration.
data.collection-secrets-encrypted#Collection:
Collection variables marked as secrets are encrypted with a per-collection AES-256-GCM key before they are written.
DB-backed collection key: ~/.local/share/gurl/keys/.key
File-backed collection key: .gurl/collections//collection.key
Git behavior: gurl init writes .gurl/.gitignore so collection.key files stay local. Commit collection.json and request files, but do not commit local collection keys.
Clone/share behavior:
Local use creates collection.key automatically when a collection secret is saved. A clone without collection.key can read non-secret collection variables and request files, but encrypted collection secrets remain locked. To share secrets, export the collection with a passphrase: gurl collection export --passphrase ... --output team.gurl. To migrate straight into shared project files, use gurl collection migrate --passphrase .... This writes passphrase-protected collection.json data and leaves no local collection.key. The receiver imports with the passphrase to re-encrypt secrets with that machine’s local collection.key, or unlocks a passphrase-protected file collection to cache the derived key in the OS keychain. Passphrase exports use PBKDF2-SHA256 with a per-export salt and AES-256-GCM for secret values. gurl collection unlock stores the derived key in the OS keychain so later commands can decrypt passphrase-protected collections without prompting again. --passphrase is available for interactive use, and GURL_IMPORT_PASSPHRASE can provide the passphrase in CI.
data.config-file#Config File:
The TOML config file at ~/.config/gurl/config.toml or ~/.gurlrc contains general settings only.
Stored settings:
history_depth (number of requests to keep in history) output_format (default output format) timeout (request timeout in seconds) log_level (logging verbosity) Never stored in config:
API keys OAuth tokens Passwords Any credential values Custom path: Set GURL_CONFIG_PATH environment variable to use a different location.
data.environment-secrets-encrypted#Environmen:
Environment variables marked --secret are encrypted before storage in both the default database and file-backed project environments under .gurl/environments/. This applies to API keys, OAuth tokens, passwords, and any other value you want protected.
Enter secrets without putting them on the command line: KEY=- reads the value from stdin, with a no-echo prompt on a terminal.
gurl env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY Algorithm: AES-256-GCM
Machine key: 256-bit key generated via crypto/rand, stored at ~/.local/share/gurl/.secret-key with permissions 0600
Nonce: 12 bytes, randomly generated per encryption operation
Important Only values marked --secret get encrypted. Regular environment variables are stored as plaintext. Mark anything sensitive.
How it works:
First launch generates a 256-bit key using crypto/rand and saves it to ~/.local/share/gurl/.secret-key File permissions are set to 0600 (owner read/write only) When you create a secret: gurl env create prod --secret "API_KEY=sk-xxx", the value is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and stored At request execution time, the key is loaded, the value is decrypted, and templates such as {{API_KEY}} can be used by request fields or auth parameters The decrypted value lives only in memory during the request Machine dependency: Because the key is stored locally, encrypted values cannot be decrypted on a different machine. If you copy your Gurl data to another machine, secrets are unreadable.
data.execution-records-no-secrets#Execution R: Every run is recorded in the same database so failures can be inspected with gurl diag. Records never contain secrets: secret and credential-looking values, literal credential headers and sensitive query parameters are masked before the record is written, as are their URL- and JSON-escaped copies in the URL, headers, body, errors and assertion messages. Response bodies are stored as received. See Secret masking.
data.security-comparison#Security Comparison: Concern Gurl CLI AI Agent Direct Handling Credentials at rest Env secrets encrypted AES-256-GCM AI might store in plaintext context Credentials in transit Applied to headers by auth handlers AI might log/expose in prompts Output and records Secrets masked as ***** (bodies too in agent mode) AI might output full headers Machine key Per-machine 256-bit key (0600) AI has no equivalent Token caching OAuth2 tokens cached in memory with TTL AI might expose cached tokens The key difference is that Gurl treats credential handling as a separate concern from request execution. Auth handlers apply credentials at the HTTP request layer, and templated auth params let saved requests refer to encrypted environment secrets instead of storing raw secret values in the request.

data: gurl replaces secret values with ***** in everything it prints or stores about a request. One set of rules (the internal/redact package) is shared by every command, so show, list --json, codegen, paste, dry runs, run --json and execution records all mask the same way.
data.execution-records-never-store-secrets#Ex: Every run is recorded so you can diagnose failures. Before a record is saved, secret variable values, literal credential headers and sensitive query parameters are masked, every occurrence of those values is scrubbed from the URL, request headers, request body, error and assertion messages, and sensitive response headers are masked. gurl diag therefore compares secret variables by origin only. Response bodies are stored as received.
data.request-logging#Request logging: The built-in logging plugin also replaces Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie and Proxy-Authorization header values with [REDACTED] in log output. The built-in user-agent plugin sets User-Agent: gurl/ when a request has none.

data.what-counts-as-a-secret#What counts as a:
A value is masked when any of these is true:
Rule Examples Its variable is marked secret in an environment or collection gurl env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY Its name looks sensitive Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, or any name containing key, secret, token, password, signature It is a literal value under a sensitive header -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-…' saved in the request It is a literal value of a sensitive query parameter https://api.example.com/v1?api_key=sk-live-… It is a literal sensitive auth param --auth-param token=…, the API key auth value, auth_code It was extracted or set by a script under a sensitive or secret name --extract access_token=jsonpath:$.token Every occurrence is replaced, not only the field it came from: if a secret appears in the URL, the body, an error message or an assertion message, it is masked there too, including its URL-escaped (%2B, +) and JSON-escaped (\", &) spellings. A secret overridden by a higher scope but still reachable through an alias is masked as well.
Values that still contain a {{placeholder}} only name a variable and stay visible, for example Authorization: Bearer {{API_KEY}}. Values shorter than 4 characters are not replaced inside free text, because that would garble unrelated text.
data.where-masking-applies#Where masking appl: Output Masked by default Notes gurl show, show --json, show --format curl yes --reveal shows literal values gurl list --json yes --reveal shows literal values gurl codegen yes --reveal includes literals; Authorization always becomes gurl paste yes --reveal includes literals gurl env show, env show --json yes --reveal shows plaintext gurl collection show --json yes gurl run --dry-run yes auth is never applied in a dry run gurl run --json URL, request headers, response headers, errors body shown as received, except in agent mode gurl run (plain) errors the body is your API’s response, printed as received Execution records (history, diag, diff, timeline) yes, before saving response bodies stored as received Agent mode everything above, plus response bodies, response headers, errors and gurl exec child output --reveal refused $ gurl show literal Name: literal Method: GET URL: http://127.0.0.1:18731/x?token=***** Headers: Authorization: ***** $ gurl codegen literal -l curl curl -X 'GET' -H 'Authorization: ' 'http://127.0.0.1:18731/x?token=*****'
